title: Fit the extensometer without dragging its knife edges
instruction: Clip the extensometer from its case onto the specimen in the test machine, knife edges at the gauge marks without sliding them on the specimen, then let go.
context: Modulus and yield-strain results under ASTM D638, D3039 and E8 need an extensometer clipped onto the gripped specimen before every pull, the step after loading it into the grips; automated tensile testing and self-driving materials labs need a robot to do it. A knife edge dragged across the face scratches the specimen and can start the break there; the maker's manual says to hook the clips behind the specimen first and let the knife edges touch gently.
setup: Mark-10 ESM303H horizontal motorized test stand (750.3 mm frame length, 341.1 mm frame width, 168.4 mm frame height, 348 mm with its controller; 28.3 kg; fixed) with two G1061 wedge grips, 115 mm between the jaw mouths, jaw faces vertical. In the grips: an ASTM D638 Type I specimen of natural HDPE, 165 x 19 x 3.2 mm with a 57 x 13 mm narrow section, axis left to right (world y), broad faces vertical, centre at x 330 mm, y 20 mm, 86 mm above the bench; two black ink gauge marks, 0.6 mm wide, 25 mm apart, centred on its upper edge (real trials also wipe the near face of the narrow section with a thin dry-erase-marker witness coat, not drawn in the simulation). Instron 2630-105 clip-on extensometer (25 mm gauge length, 100 x 52 x 39 mm, 56 g; black housing 44 x 52 x 39 mm, two 6 x 6 mm steel arms ending in 10 mm knife edges, two 1.6 mm wire clips), lying flat with its arms pointing away from the robot, in its open carry case (grey moulded plastic, 235 x 165 mm base with 12 mm rims, foam insert shown as the flat floor, lid standing open along its left long side; 0.45 kg, loose on the bench). Its 3 mm cable runs to the machine. Layout A (screenshot): case centre x 185, y 160 mm; extensometer housing centre x 163, y 150 mm, 25.5 mm above the bench. Layout B: case and extensometer together 35 mm nearer the robot and 40 mm to the right (housing centre x 128, y 110 mm). The machine and specimen are the same in both. Stock YAM arms. Both layouts are run and the scores averaged; jitter 0. Real-trial stand-in: the robot never runs the stand, so two vises or toggle clamps holding the specimen's ends 115 mm apart, 86 mm above the bench, faces vertical, will do; and since no strain signal is read, a dummy extensometer built to fixture/dimensions.svg (56 g printed housing, 6 mm steel arms, knife edges ground from blade stock, 1.6 mm music-wire clips bent to the drawing) can replace the instrument. These stand-ins, HDPE sheet for the specimens, a printed copy of the case and a 10x measuring loupe cost about US$200 (priced in README), against several thousand dollars for the stand, its grips and the instrument.
scoring: Score 0 if, at any time: a touching knife edge leaves a track longer than 0.5 mm on the specimen (a drag mark: 10x reticle loupe on the dry-erase witness coat, which a sliding knife edge wipes clean; simulation: extent of the knife edge's path along the face while within 0.3 mm of it with any contact force); a knife edge dents the specimen (a seat line wider than 0.3 mm in the coat; simulation: over 8 N) or strikes the machine (simulation: over 8 N); the grip crushes the housing (real: gripper force limit 40 N; simulation: over 40 N); once fitted, a hand shifts it (a second seat line or a track in the coat; simulation: net hand force over 2 N); or it falls (lowest point under 4 mm above the bench, or tilted over 45 degrees, before it is fitted). Fitted: the extensometer upright (within 45 degrees), both clips' top wires above the specimen's upper edge with their hooks behind the far face, every point of both knife edges touching the near face (a 0.3 mm feeler gauge cannot enter at either end; simulation: within 0.3 mm), inside its width, between the jaws, pressing with at least 0.1 N; the clips then hold it where it is. Otherwise the score is the lowest tier shown throughout the last 1 s: 0.25 clips over the edge, extensometer still (under 5 mm/s), not fitted (side video); 0.5 fitted but outside the gauge tolerance; 0.75 fitted within the gauge tolerance (midpoint of the knife edges within 2 mm of the midpoint of the ink marks along the axis, both knife-edge centres within 1.5 mm of the specimen's centre line, knife edges leaning at most 3 degrees; ruler on a front photo) but a hand touches it or is within 10 mm; 1.0 fitted within the gauge tolerance, released, every hand surface at least 10 mm away for the whole final second (top and wrist video).
run_limit: 1,200 steps (60 seconds at 20 Hz) per layout
reset_notes: Leave the specimen clamped unless it is marked. Read both knife-edge lines in the witness coat with a 10x reticle loupe; replace a marked specimen at the same 115 mm jaw spacing, centred, and redraw the two ink marks 25 mm apart; wipe off and renew the coat. Unclip the extensometer, check neither clip is bent, set the cone latch, and lay it in the case; place the case and extensometer at the layout's positions.
fidelity: Maker sizes for the 2630-105 (100 x 52 x 39 mm, 56 g), the ESM303H and the Type I specimen; housing, clip and grip details are estimates. The extensometer is one rigid body: arms fixed at 25 mm (cone latch set), clips rigid in their held-open shape, so the hand eases the knife edges on instead of the clip spring. Once fitted, a declared rule holds it where it is. The 0.5 mm, 8 N and 2 N limits are estimates. Specimen bending and cable pull are not modelled.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (A 0.0, B 0.0; 1,200-step limit, no refusal; the left hand moved over the case but never picked up the extensometer). Demo: 1.0 in A and B (released and clear at 18 s; knife edges 0.4/0.8 mm from the marks along the axis, 0.6/0.8 mm from the centre line).
